title: Sustainability and Packaging Trends in Health, Beauty, and Wellness
summary: Sustainable packaging trends now carry filing dates. See the formats, the honest tradeoffs, and the SKU-level data behind EPR reporting.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


What each sustainable format costs in money, adoption, and freight


-


Where extended producer responsibility rules stand as of August 2026


-


Why packaging reports depend on accurate product and packaging attribute data


---


Sustainable packaging trends in health, beauty, and wellness used to be purely a marketing decision, but now are beholden to a filing calendar. As of August 2026, seven US states have passed packaging extended producer responsibility (EPR) laws, with most producer reports due each May. Meanwhile, the European Union's Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) took effect on Aug. 12, 2026.


Choosing a refillable format is still a design and branding decision; however, it’s also now a data decision. Every packaging component has to be reported by material and by weight, for every stock-keeping unit (SKU). The accuracy of that report rests on records that might not have been built to handle this sort of data.


## What Is Driving Sustainable Packaging Trends Right Now?


### The Consumer Driver Is Real but Uneven


GlobalData surveyed 22,613 people across 42 countries in the last quarter of 2025. It found that[74% treat sustainable attributes as essential or nice to have](https://www.cosmeticsdesign-europe.com/Article/2026/03/04/refillable-beauty-a-key-growth-strategy-for-makeup-brands/) . Another 73% actively look for products that cut packaging waste.


But studies also indicate that shopper patience is thinning too. Mintel's 2026 packaging predictions note that people have caught on that[recyclable does not mean recycled](https://beautymatter.com/articles/the-beauty-packaging-trends-set-to-define-2026) , and that vague words like “eco-friendly” don't seem to reliably indicate anything meaningful.

## How Is Regulation Reshaping Sustainable Packaging Strategy?


A sustainable packaging strategy now has to survive an audit, in which four kinds of rules matter most.


-


**Extended producer responsibility:** EPR makes the company that puts packaging on the market pay fees based on how much packaging was sold and what it is made of, with those fees funding collection and recycling. Seven states have passed these laws: Maine, Oregon, California, Colorado, Minnesota, Maryland, and Washington. Bills are pending in four more.


-


**Recyclability labeling:** The chasing-arrows triangle on plastic packaging reads to shoppers as "recyclable," but the number inside it only identifies the plastic. California's[SB 343](https://calrecycle.ca.gov/wcs/recyclinglabels/) mandates that packaging failing state recyclability criteria can no longer carry the arrows, which means new artwork for anything that does not qualify. Industry groups sued in federal court in March 2026 to block it, and the court has not ruled.


-


**Recycled-content mandates:** Five states have set a minimum for post-consumer recycled content in plastic packaging. Each state requires an annual report, with the targets rising over time, reaching 50% for beverage containers in several states by the early 2030s.


-


**The EU packaging regulation.**[The PPWR came into effect on Aug. 12, 2026](https://www.omm.com/insights/alerts-publications/2026-plastics-epr-packaging-rules-update-what-sb-54-sb-343-state-reporting-deadlines-prc-laws-the-eu-ppwr-mean-for-producers-retailers/) . It requires all packaging to be recyclable in an economically viable way by 2030, sets rising reuse targets, bans a group of chemicals known as PFAS in food packaging, and strengthens EPR obligations.


### Where Things Stand as of August 2026


These rules are live but not settled. A federal court granted a preliminary injunction against Oregon's EPR law in February 2026, and Maine received no bids to operate its program.[Packaging Dive maintains a running deadline tracker](https://www.packagingdive.com/news/extended-producer-responsibility-packaging-laws-regulations-calendar/727548/) worth checking before relying on any date here.


## Why Is Refillable Packaging Still Hard To Scale?


At the premium end, refillable packaging is growing. L'Oreal, for instance, expanded refills across Lancome and Yves Saint Laurent lipstick and foundation ranges in Europe in June 2025 and priced them as a premium option. Meanwhile, LVMH launched La Beaute by Louis Vuitton in autumn 2025 with refillable cases positioned as heirlooms.


But the execution is difficult. Refill systems["must match, or ideally exceed, the convenience of purchasing a new product,"](https://www.personalcareinsights.com/news/beauty-packaging-trends-report.html) and any extra hassle hinders repeat use. The other barriers are structural:


-


Hygiene, since a refill has to prevent contamination without worsening the experience.


-


Reverse logistics, in-store systems, or refill stations, all of which add operational cost.


-


Inconsistent retail support, which slows uptake even when a brand is committed.


-


Cost, in tooling the durable package and in running the refill program.


Scale does not make these problems disappear. L'Oreal missed both of its 2025 packaging targets. Per its 2024 annual filing,[49% of its packaging met the recyclable, reusable, refillable, or compostable goal against a target of 100%, and 37% was recycled or bio-based against a target of 50%](https://packagingeurope.com/news/where-loreal-stands-after-missing-sustainable-packaging-goals-for-2025/12739.article) . Both targets are restated for 2030.


Smaller brands use material choice to stand out instead. Aluminum, for instance, was a breakout beauty material in 2025, picked up by brands including Dieux, Experiment Beauty, and Grown Alchemist.


## How Does a Packaging Change Ripple Through the Sustainable Packaging Supply Chain?


A packaging change is rarely just that, and can often have consequences beyond the packaging itself.


### New Formats Become New Item Data


A new material or format changes dimensions, weights, case packs, and sometimes the Global Trade Item Number. Those values feed item setup, retailer product content, warehouse slotting, and freight quoting. Material and recycled-content attributes become product data that retailers now ask for.


Compliance works the same way. John Blake, senior director analyst at Gartner, told BeautyMatter that packaging legislation compliance is["fully reliant on accurate specification data,"](https://beautymatter.com/articles/the-beauty-packaging-trends-set-to-define-2026) which is pushing companies to close gaps in data quality and governance.


### Refill and Take-Back Add Reverse Flows


Refill and take-back models send packaging back the other direction. That means returns handling, inspection, and reconciliation at volumes most beauty brands have never run. Scaling these systems depends on making them cheaper and better tied into how stores already work.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the biggest sustainable packaging trends in beauty right now?


Refillable formats, recycled content, mono-material designs, aluminum, and waterless products. Additionally, brands are being asked to document what packaging is made of, SKU by SKU, for regulatory reports.


### Does extended producer responsibility apply to my brand?


That depends on where you sell, your revenue, and how each state defines a producer. Thresholds and exemptions vary. Your sustainability and legal teams should double-check what you owe.


### Is refillable packaging actually better for the environment?


It can be, and the size of the benefit depends on how often someone refills. Habit matters more than the format. That is why more brands now measure refill rates instead of assuming them.


### What packaging data do EPR reports usually require?


Usually the material type and weight of each packaging component, tied to the products you sold in that state during the reporting period. Rules differ by program, so double-check the fields against the one you registered with.
